questions.q: What is an expense report template?
options: A business-unit-scoped set of expense types an employee can choose from, carrying default accounting information
A PDF receipt attached to an expense report
A single dollar limit applied company-wide
The approval workflow for an expense report
questions.explain: A template defines which expense types are available to a business unit's employees and carries default accounting so items distribute automatically.

questions.q: What is the relationship between an expense category and an expense type?
options: They are the exact same thing with two different names
A category is a seeded grouping (like Accommodations) that contains one or more specific expense types (like Hotel, Motel)
A category is defined by the employee at submission time
An expense type can belong to multiple templates but never to a category
questions.explain: Categories are system-defined groupings that drive behavior; specific expense types the employee actually picks live nested inside a category.

questions.q: Why does a category like Accommodations matter beyond organizing the list of types?
options: It has no functional effect at all
The category sets the employee's salary
The category drives system behavior such as itemization eligibility and corporate card feed eligibility
The category determines the company's fiscal year
questions.explain: The category-level behavior governs things like whether itemization or card capture applies, even though each expense type can have its own policy limit.

questions.q: When an employee selects an expense type like Hotel, what has the template already determined, without the employee doing anything?
options: The employee's manager
The employee's base salary
The company's legal entity structure
The default GL account, receipt requirement, itemization requirement, and reimbursability
questions.explain: Templates default accounting and behavioral attributes so employees never have to pick a GL account combination themselves.

questions.q: In the worked example, what was the first step before adding 'Parking' as a new expense type for Field Services?
options: Immediately rewriting the Hotel policy limit
Checking whether Parking already exists as a seeded expense type under Ground Transportation
Deleting the Field Services business unit
Creating an entirely new chart of accounts
questions.explain: Because Parking is typically a seeded expense type already, the first step is checking whether it needs to be activated rather than created from scratch.
